b176924381.why: With an unconstrained XOR mask and all vector results live, the SSE2 loads, XORs, averages, stores, and scalar updates have no removable step.

ff3d923285.why: The vertical averages already share their transformed source rows, and all remaining results and updates are required.

3ccf53a804.why: The transformed rows are already reused across adjacent averages, and preserving every final vector register prevents eliminating the remaining operations.

3340f39e27.why: The two bounded loads, byte interleave, and PMADDUBSW compute the eight exact sums, while both constant registers and scalar updates remain live.

9b15dd68c1.why: Both constant registers must be retained, and the two eight-byte loads, interleave, multiply-add, and scalar updates are already tight.

0b70835358.why: SSE2 requires both input halves to be widened before producing the exact word sums, and the zero register, constant register, and scalar updates are live.

495151151d.why: The exact byte-pair sums require the existing widening and addition sequence under SSE2, with both output halves and initialization results preserved.

bbeb591c5d.why: Both PMADDUBSW results and both constant registers are live, and exchanging the unsigned input bytes with the signed multiplier operand would change the sums.

2ef98d5a36.why: Broadcasting the low word from EDX requires the three SSE2 operations, and preserving doubled ECX and the masked zero flag requires both scalar operations.

31ea29674e.why: XMM1 and XMM3 must retain their loaded values, so SSE2 memory-operand additions would require replacement copies and save no instructions.

f850d06986.why: The original destination vectors in XMM1 and XMM3 are live, and destructive SSE2 additions cannot eliminate the source loads without adding copies.

bfdbeae857.why: AVX2 needs a separate GPR-to-vector move before the word broadcast, while the doubled counter and masked zero flag require separate operations.
